{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Base Terms — 18 rules assessed 

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Eight clauses are compliant (several better than our preferred position), eight are deviations requiring redline, and two rules have no usable clause at all.

The commercial shape of the deal is broadly acceptable: there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-purchase commitment, non-solicit or audit right imposed on us; governing law is New York with no arbitration; and the Vendor-side IP indemnity in § 8.1 sits at our fallback with indemnification payments carved out of the cap.

The problems cluster in three areas. First, **IP and licence**: § 7.0 defaults all deliverables to Type II (IBM-owned) Materials with a narrow intra-Enterprise licence back, and the § 12.1 Base Components licence is expressly *revocable* and runs to Customer only — no Affiliates or contractors. Second, **liability and warranty**: the caps in §§ 9.1/9.2 are mutual and on an acceptable basis, but carve-outs for confidentiality/data, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement are absent, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM liability for loss of our records or data outright; § 5.1 offers only a workmanlike-standard warranty which § 5.4(c) then swallows with an unqualified "AS IS". Third, **exit**: our § 3.4 convenience right is conditioned on uncapped early termination charges defined outside this document, § 3.2 auto-renews for a term equal to the previous term on 90 days' notice with no uplift cap, and there is no transition assistance, Content return or deletion obligation anywhere. There is also no insurance clause of any kind, despite IBM hosting our Content and processing personal information under § 14.18.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | At fallback; indemnity payments carved out of the cap under § 9.1(a). Preferred non-IP heads absent (noted only). |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (§ 7.0 Materials) | Type II default gives IBM title; licence back excludes modification/sublicensing and is limited to our Enterprise. Flip default to Type I and confirm Content ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Caps mutual and acceptable, but no carve-outs for confidentiality/data, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP; § 9.1(c)(2) excludes data/records liability. Add mutual § 9.3 carve-outs. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14.10 Assignment | One-sided: consent gate binds us only, IBM assignment unrestricted. Make mutual, add competitor bar and affiliate/asset-sale carve-out. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No exclusivity or requirements obligation; § 14.16 preserves freedom to contract with others. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Early termination charges set in Attachment A, uncapped and not reproduced here. Cap at three months' charges and make sole remedy. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 12.1 License | Grant is "revocable" with no cause standard and excludes Affiliates and contractors; § 14.17 forecloses implied extension. Remove revocability at will and extend scope. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant; § 14.11 No Resale is an ordinary redistribution limit. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | One month's notice and no IBM convenience right meet preferred position, but uncapped exit charges (§ 3.4(b)) and no refund of prepaid Charges (§ 3.5) fail the fallback. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | No audit, inspection or system-access right; better than preferred. § 11.3 cooperation duty noted only. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York law, no arbitration. Silence on exclusive venue is a sub-element, noted not redlined. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No MFN obligation on us; § 14.16 confirms the opposite. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | Charges for ordered Services only; monthly exit right. Attachments to be checked for take-or-pay pricing. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.8 Personnel | No no-hire or non-solicit covenant. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 3.2 Renewal | Renews for a term equal to the previous term, 90 days' notice, no uplift cap or reminder. Move to 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, reminder and CPI/3% cap. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | No transition, Content return, export or deletion language anywhere. Insert six months' assistance, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion (90-day fallback available). |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Workmanlike standard only; no conformance or no-malicious-code warranty, no period, no remedy, and § 5.4(c) puts Materials "AS IS". Add 90-day warranty with remedy and carve out of the disclaimer. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance obligation at all despite IBM hosting Content and processing personal information (§ 14.18). Insert § 14.12A (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp, certificates). |

---

## Walk-away items

These three points fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature, not trading chips:

1. **§ 12.1 licence revocable at IBM's discretion, Customer-only (LICENSE).** A revocable-at-will grant with no Affiliate or contractor coverage, reinforced by § 14.17, is not a usable licence. Minimum acceptable outcome: revocation limited to our uncured material breach, with Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf covered.
2. **§ 3.2 auto-renewal for a term equal to the previous term (RENEWAL).** A multi-year initial term that rolls into a further multi-year term on 90 days' notice, with no cap on renewal Charge increases, is walk-away territory. Minimum acceptable outcome: 12-month renewals with a 30-day opt-out (60 days with a 5% uplift cap is the fallback landing zone).
3. **No insurance whatsoever (INSURANCE).** IBM hosts our Content and processes personal information on our behalf under § 14.18; a hosting vendor with no coverage at all is the rule's walk-away scenario rather than a shortfall. Fallback landing zone: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

We also flag, short of walk-away, that the combination of uncapped Attachment A early termination charges (§ 3.4(b)) and the absence of any transition or data-return obligation (§ 3.5) can make our convenience right economically illusory and leave our Content stranded. These should be resolved together.

---

## Next steps

1. **Obtain the missing documents before we finalise our position.** Attachment A and each Service Option Attachment drive the early termination charges (§ 3.4(b)) and would also be where any minimum-volume or take-or-pay pricing sits. We cannot close out LD, T4C or MINCOMMIT without them.
2. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations and two missing clauses: Type I Materials default plus a Content ownership statement; a new mutual § 9.3 carve-out provision leaving the existing caps intact; mutual assignment in § 14.10; a three-month cap and sole-remedy wording on early termination charges plus pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges; § 12.1 licence scope and revocability; § 3.2 renewal mechanics; a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty carved out of § 5.4(c); § 3.5 transition, return and certified deletion; and new § 14.12A insurance.
3. **Sequence the negotiation** around the three walk-away items first (licence scope, renewal, insurance), then the critical IP and liability carve-out points, then the exit economics package. Where we have identified a fallback (renewal at 60 days/5%; transition at 90 days plus 30-day export; insurance at E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M; early termination charges capped at three months), we have authority to land there.
4. **Confirm we do not reopen the compliant clauses.** The eight compliant findings — including the § 8.1 indemnity at fallback and the absence of audit, exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment and non-solicit obligations — are at or better than our position and should be left alone.
5. **Record the noted-only items** (venue silence in § 14.3, absence of preferred non-IP indemnity heads, the § 11.3 information-provision duty, late payment fees under § 4.2) in the deal file so they are not raised as issues in this round."}
